requirement:
Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.
rationale:
**Obligations.** The requirement says the setup-generated coverage documentation and the bundled agent instructions must explain five things:
1. How to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose justification.
2. How to author or refresh its citation review using `habeas author`.
3. That the anchor needs no project declaration or exception-specific configuration.
4. That only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception.
5. That ordinary partially uncovered functions need no exception when their file meets its target.

The implementing sources are the `GUIDANCE` const in `src/execution_coverage.rs`, which supplies the generated coverage page, and the "Testing and coverage artifacts" paragraph of `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`. I read both. I also read the `md/reference.md` built-in definitions paragraph that carries an `{impl}` reference. It is the project's own book rather than setup-generated or bundled material, so I did not require it to be tested.

**Generated coverage documentation.** The test `generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` builds a book fixture and runs `populate_in`. It asserts that the generated coverage chapter contains these phrases:
- `habeas:coverage` (obligation 1)
- "substantive prose justification" (obligation 1)
- "fenced commentary or a Rust doc comment" (obligation 1)
- "citation review with `habeas author`" (obligation 2)
- "No project declaration or special configuration" (obligation 3)
- "current accepted review" (obligation 4)
- "Ordinary partly covered functions need no exception when their file meets its target" (obligation 5)

It runs once with numbered sections and once without. A regression that dropped any of these explanations would fail the test.

**Bundled agent instructions.** The test `shared_agent_guidance_documents_post_suite_checks_and_standard_explanations` in `tests/repository.rs` reads `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` and asserts these phrases:
- the standard `{cite}` of `habeas:coverage` (obligation 1)
- "rationale in fenced commentary or a Rust doc comment" (obligation 1)
- "citation review with `habeas author`" (obligation 2)
- "Only current accepted review evidence permits the exception" (obligation 4)
- "No project declaration or extra configuration is needed" (obligation 3)
- "Partly covered functions need no exception when their file meets its target" (obligation 5)

**Setup test.** `coverage_setup_is_idempotent_and_hook_needs_no_coverage_chapter` in `tests/setup.rs` is also marked `{test}` for this requirement. It does not assert guidance text. It checks that setup creates no coverage chapter and that the generated configuration is idempotent. It adds nothing to the assessment, and it does not weaken it either.

**Unresolved wording.** "Author or refresh" is not tested as a separate phrase. The guidance only says to author the review with `habeas author`, and the tests assert that. "Refresh" uses the same command, so I do not treat it as a distinct obligation or a gap.

**Conclusion.** Every obligation is covered by a test that asserts concrete content in both the generated documentation and the bundled instructions. I found no marking or assertion gaps.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions.setup
Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
